page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32g-240s is a memory-optimized instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute series, provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside support for vector instructions such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic extensions including AES and SHA-NI. System memory totals 32.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for workloads requiring substantial RAM allocation without requiring extensive thread parallelism. Storage is locally attached as a 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes a complimentary public IPv4 address without bundled GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded computational capabilities alongside balanced memory bandwidth. The instance achieves a top 25 percent stress-ng single-core score of 3056.38, top 10 percent Geekbench text processing score of 2841.0, and single-threaded gzip throughput of 33.72 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth metrics measure 70.47 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 41.18 GB/sec for write operations. However, aggregate multi-core throughput reflects the physical limit of 2 dedicated execution cores; the Geekbench multi-core score registers at 4251.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 29.72 GB/sec, placing overall parallel computing output in lower percentiles.

The high memory-to-core density provides a cost-effective operational profile for stateful services that would otherwise require over-provisioning compute resources merely to acquire sufficient memory capacity. In caching environments, the instance executes 6.88 million Redis SET operations per second and sustains static web throughput of 12.55 GB/sec. It is functionally configured for relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, text parsing tasks, and moderate web applications, but is unsuited for heavy parallel compilations or large-scale machine learning training.
description: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32g-240s is a memory-optimized virtual server featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs backed by 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 32.0 GB of system memory and 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and 32 MB of L3 cache, the hardware achieves an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Single-threaded metrics are strong, with top-tier results in text processing and compression, while large-block read memory bandwidth reaches 70.47 GB/sec. Conversely, the 2-core boundary constrains multi-threaded compilation and heavy parallel processing workloads. The hardware configuration delivers high RAM density per compute unit, presenting an efficient foundation for in-memory databases, Redis caches, text indexing pipelines, and moderate web workloads requiring high capacity without redundant core provisioning.
